title: Decrypt String from Alphabet to Integer Mapping
summary: Given a string s consisting of digits and '#', map each digit or digit-pair to its corresponding English lowercase character ('1' to '9' maps to 'a' to 'i', and '10#' to '26#' maps to 'j' to 'z').
statement: Given a string s consisting of digits and '#', map each digit or digit-pair to its corresponding English lowercase character ('1' to '9' maps to 'a' to 'i', and '10#' to '26#' maps to 'j' to 'z'). Return the resulting string after the mapping.
constraints: 1..9 map to a..i and 10#..26# map to j..z.
reference_solution:
def decrypt_alphabet_string(s):
 answer='';i=len(s)-1
 while i>=0:
  if s[i]=='#':value=int(s[i-2:i]);i-=3
  else:value=int(s[i]);i-=1
  answer=chr(96+value)+answer
 return answer
hints: Parse from right to left because # unambiguously marks a two-digit token.
On # read the preceding two digits; otherwise read one digit.
Convert 1..26 to letters and prepend or reverse the result.
Every suffix has exactly one valid next token under this grammar.
editorial: Every suffix has exactly one valid next token under this grammar.
